log.text: Liftoff. Mars in the window: 18° right. Fuel for 62 s of burn.
Out of the dense air: altitude 36, speed 16 u/s.
Meteor M-2 in the window (29° right, 12% of Mars's light). The pilot held its course.
Meteor M-7 in the window (5° left, 12% of Mars's light). The pilot held its course.
Target centred in the window (-4°). DNp20: right 35 Hz, left 0 Hz.
Meteor M-4 in the window (18° right, 30% of Mars's light). The pilot held its course.
Flight computer: flip, engines first. Altitude 165, closing 40 u/s. The pilot's lever is off for the manoeuvre.
Target held centred for 5.7 s without a break.
Meteor M-3 in the window (4° left, 30% of Mars's light). The pilot turned toward its light: the target slid to 135° left.
Flip complete, landing burn. The pilot now looks through the landing camera; its lever moves the rocket sideways.
The pad never came to the centre of the camera: closest 8° left.
Flight computer: altitude 20. Below this the sideways speed is limited in proportion to height; the direction stays the pilot's.
Touchdown: 1.5 u/s down, 0.3 u/s sideways, ground slope 24°, 5.8 u from the centre of the pad.

The legs' signal reached 2,522 leg mechanosensory neurons. In 0.5 s the ascending neurons (legs → brain) fired 16,567 spikes, against 0 before contact. Strongest in the brain: PEN_a(PEN1) (+1,817), PEN_b(PEN2) (+1,710), cells with no named type (+1,437).

cause: CAUSE: the rocket tipped over after touchdown — ground slope 24°, above the 12° the legs can stand on. The pad was 6 u away.
